segments.text: What happens? The community assembles as the ministers enter and the opening chant or song begins.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Bring your whole life into worship: your work, relationships, gratitude, and unanswered questions. Faith grows in a community that receives each person as someone God calls by name.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Arrive a few minutes early. Put away distractions, notice the altar, and make space for a quiet intention. Join the singing as you are able.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Everyone: The entrance chant or hymn selected for this Mass. Use the parish worship aid for its words.
segments.label: Everyone

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The entrance song or antiphon varies. There is no single fixed spoken response here.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? We acknowledge our need for mercy and ask the Lord to heal us.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Honest repentance allows grace to reach the places we prefer to hide. Christian conversion involves responsibility for our actions together with trust that God desires our restoration.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Use the silence to name a concrete failure and ask for mercy. Join the responses with hope. Seek sacramental Reconciliation when needed.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words: The priest chooses one of the approved forms. Use the form led at your parish.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text:
Everyone, Form A (Confiteor): I confess to almighty God
and to you, my brothers and sisters,
that I have greatly sinned,
in my thoughts and in my words,
in what I have done and in what I have failed to do,
through my fault, through my fault,
through my most grievous fault;
therefore I ask blessed Mary ever-Virgin,
all the Angels and Saints,
and you, my brothers and sisters,
to pray for me to the Lord our God.
segments.label: Everyone · Form A (Confiteor)

segments.text: Priest, Form B: Have mercy on us, O Lord.
segments.label: Priest · Form B

segments.text: We respond, Form B: For we have sinned against you.
segments.label: We respond · Form B

segments.text: Priest, Form B: Show us, O Lord, your mercy.
segments.label: Priest · Form B

segments.text: We respond, Form B: And grant us your salvation.
segments.label: We respond · Form B

segments.text: Minister, Form C: Invocations addressed to Christ precede each Lord, have mercy or Christ, have mercy response. The invocations vary.
segments.label: Minister · Form C

segments.text:
We respond, Kyrie (minister leads each line): Lord, have mercy.
Christ, have mercy.
Lord, have mercy.
segments.label: We respond · Kyrie (minister leads each line)

segments.text:
We respond, Greek alternative (minister leads each line): Kyrie, eleison.
Christe, eleison.
Kyrie, eleison.
segments.label: We respond · Greek alternative (minister leads each line)

segments.text: Priest: A prayer asking for mercy, forgiveness, and everlasting life.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: We respond: Amen.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The Kyrie follows unless it has already been included. It may be sung or said in Greek. A sprinkling rite can replace the Penitential Act; follow its prayer and song.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? A reader proclaims the First Reading, usually from the Old Testament. During the Easter season, it is normally from the Acts of the Apostles in the New Testament.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Listen for God’s faithfulness across generations. The stories of Israel invite us to consider how God forms a people through promises, deliverance, and the patient work of conversion.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Sit and listen. At the usual conclusion, respond: “Thanks be to God.” Read the Sunday passages before Mass if you can.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Reader: Proclaims the first reading assigned for the day.
segments.label: Reader

segments.text: Reader, conclusion: The word of the Lord.
segments.label: Reader · conclusion

segments.text: We respond: Thanks be to God.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: Readings for the celebration: Find the assigned Scripture readings, Psalm response, and Gospel acclamation for the day.
segments.label: Readings for the celebration

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The reading itself varies. The reader announces its conclusion as the word of the Lord.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The community welcomes the Gospel with an acclamation.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Welcoming Christ’s word calls for receptivity. A short sung response can help us turn from passive observation to a deliberate willingness to hear and follow.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Stand as you are able and join the acclamation. In Lent, notice the different acclamation used.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Everyone, outside Lent: Alleluia.
segments.label: Everyone · outside Lent

segments.text: Cantor: The Gospel verse assigned for this Mass.
segments.label: Cantor

segments.text: Everyone, repeat outside Lent: Alleluia.
segments.label: Everyone · repeat outside Lent

segments.text: Everyone, during Lent: The Lenten Gospel acclamation printed in the worship aid.
segments.label: Everyone · during Lent

segments.text: Readings for the celebration: Find the assigned Scripture readings, Psalm response, and Gospel acclamation for the day.
segments.label: Readings for the celebration

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The verse and Lenten acclamation vary. Alleluia is not sung or said during Lent.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? On Sundays and solemnities, the assembly ordinarily professes the Creed.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Faith involves both personal trust and belonging to a community that hands on what it has received. The Creed offers a framework for study and a place to name honest questions.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Follow the text in the parish worship aid. Bring unfamiliar phrases to OCIA; understanding grows through prayer, conversation, and study.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text:
Everyone, Nicene Creed: I believe in one God, the Father almighty,
maker of heaven and earth,
of all things visible and invisible.
I believe in one Lord Jesus Christ,
the Only Begotten Son of God,
born of the Father before all ages.
God from God, Light from Light,
true God from true God,
begotten, not made, consubstantial with the Father;
through him all things were made.
For us men and for our salvation
he came down from heaven,
and by the Holy Spirit was incarnate
of the Virgin Mary,
and became man.
For our sake he was crucified under Pontius Pilate,
he suffered death and was buried,
and rose again on the third day
in accordance with the Scriptures.
He ascended into heaven
and is seated at the right hand of the Father.
He will come again in glory
to judge the living and the dead
and his kingdom will have no end.
I believe in the Holy Spirit,
the Lord, the giver of life,
who proceeds from the Father and the Son,
who with the Father and the Son
is adored and glorified,
who has spoken through the prophets.
I believe in one, holy, catholic and apostolic Church.
I confess one Baptism for the forgiveness of sins
and I look forward to the resurrection of the dead
and the life of the world to come. Amen.
segments.label: Everyone · Nicene Creed

segments.text: Everyone, approved alternative: Apostles’ Creed, especially in Lent and Easter.
segments.label: Everyone · approved alternative

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The Creed concludes with Amen. All bow at the words about the Incarnation; on Christmas and the Annunciation, all genuflect at those words. A renewal of baptismal promises replaces the Creed in certain celebrations.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The priest invites prayer and concludes the preparation of the gifts.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? An offering makes room for gratitude and surrender. Ask God to receive your life and teach you to give freely, especially where generosity feels difficult.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Join the invitation and listen to the prayer. Respond Amen attentively.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Priest: Pray, brethren, that my sacrifice and yours may be acceptable to God, the almighty Father.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text:
We respond: May the Lord accept the sacrifice at your hands
for the praise and glory of his name,
for our good
and the good of all his holy Church.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: Priest: The Prayer over the Offerings appointed for the day.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: We respond: Amen.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The priest’s prayer changes with the day.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The prayer invokes the Holy Spirit and recounts Christ’s words and actions at the Last Supper.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? By the power of Christ’s word and the Holy Spirit, bread and wine become his Body and Blood. The Church calls this change transubstantiation: appearances remain, while Christ is truly, really, and substantially present.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Adore quietly. Bring questions about the Real Presence to your catechist; take time to study and pray rather than rushing toward a conclusion.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Priest: Epiclesis: the invocation of the Holy Spirit over the gifts.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: Priest: Institution narrative and words of consecration over the bread and wine.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: We participate: Listen and adore in silence. There is no prescribed spoken congregational response during the consecration.
segments.label: We participate

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The wording of these prayers differs between Eucharistic Prayers; the priest uses the prayer selected for this celebration. The memorial acclamation follows in the next lesson.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The assembly prays the prayer Jesus taught his disciples.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Naming God as Father invites trust and recognizes others as brothers and sisters. Asking for bread and forgiveness touches both our deepest needs and the way we treat our neighbors.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Pray the familiar words slowly enough to notice one petition. Follow local guidance about posture.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Priest: At the Savior's command and formed by divine teaching, we dare to say:
segments.label: Priest
Everyone · Our Father

segments.text: Priest: Embolism: the prayer for deliverance from evil and for peace.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text:
Everyone, after the priest’s prayer: For the kingdom,
the power and the glory are yours
now and for ever.
segments.label: Everyone · after the priest’s prayer

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. At Mass, do not add Amen immediately after the Our Father. The priest’s prayer follows, and then the people give the concluding acclamation from the Order of Mass.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? Those properly prepared receive Christ sacramentally; others remain in prayer.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Communion unites the recipient with Christ and his Church. Receiving calls for faith, sacramental preparation, and a disposition of grace. An OCIA lesson or completed course does not itself establish readiness to receive.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? If you have not yet been admitted to Communion, remain in prayer and speak with your OCIA team. Those receiving follow parish directions and answer Amen to the minister.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text:
Priest: Behold the Lamb of God,
behold him who takes away the sins of the world.
Blessed are those called to the supper of the Lamb.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text:
Everyone: Lord, I am not worthy
that you should enter under my roof,
but only say the word
and my soul shall be healed.
segments.label: Everyone

segments.text: Minister, when offering the host: The Body of Christ.
segments.label: Minister · when offering the host

segments.text: Person receiving: Amen.
segments.label: Person receiving

segments.text: Minister, when offering the chalice: The Blood of Christ.
segments.label: Minister · when offering the chalice

segments.text: Person receiving: Amen.
segments.label: Person receiving

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The Communion chant or hymn varies. Those not receiving Communion remain in prayer; no spoken response to a minister is required from them.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The dismissal sends the assembly to live what it has celebrated.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Worship bears fruit in love of neighbor. Choose an achievable act of discipleship: contact someone isolated, serve a person in need, keep a difficult promise, or make time for prayer.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Respond “Thanks be to God.” Before leaving, choose one concrete way to live the Gospel this week.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text:
Deacon or priest, one of these dismissals: Go forth, the Mass is ended.
OR Go and announce the Gospel of the Lord.
OR Go in peace, glorifying the Lord by your life.
OR Go in peace.
segments.label: Deacon or priest · one of these dismissals

segments.text: We respond: Thanks be to God.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. A concluding hymn may follow and changes with the parish or occasion. During the Easter Octave and on Pentecost, a double Alleluia is added to the dismissal and the people’s response.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The celebration begins in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? This familiar gesture names the Trinity and places our prayer under the sign of Christ’s saving Cross. Repeating it slowly can become a daily reminder that Christian life belongs to God.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? In Latin Catholic practice, use your right hand: forehead, chest, left shoulder, right shoulder. Pray attentively rather than rushing the gesture.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Priest, everyone makes the gesture: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
segments.label: Priest · everyone makes the gesture

segments.text: We respond: Amen.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: What happens? On appointed days, the assembly sings or says a hymn of praise.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Praise teaches us to look beyond our immediate needs and delight in God’s goodness. Consider what it means to worship God even when life is difficult or an answer to prayer seems distant.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Join the hymn when it is used. Let its movement from praise to petition draw your attention to Christ.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text:
Everyone, Gloria: Glory to God in the highest,
and on earth peace to people of good will.
We praise you,
we bless you,
we adore you,
we glorify you,
we give you thanks for your great glory,
Lord God, heavenly King,
O God, almighty Father.
Lord Jesus Christ, Only Begotten Son,
Lord God, Lamb of God, Son of the Father,
you take away the sins of the world,
have mercy on us;
you take away the sins of the world,
receive our prayer;
you are seated at the right hand of the Father,
have mercy on us.
For you alone are the Holy One,
you alone are the Lord,
you alone are the Most High,
Jesus Christ,
with the Holy Spirit,
in the glory of God the Father.
Amen.
segments.label: Everyone · Gloria

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The whole hymn is sung or recited when prescribed. It ends with Amen. It is ordinarily omitted in Advent and Lent, with exceptions for prescribed celebrations.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The assembly responds to the reading with a psalm, often sung.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? The Psalms give us language for joy, fear, anger, trust, and sorrow. They allow prayer to be honest while gradually directing our attention toward God.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Listen to each verse and join the refrain. Carry one phrase into the coming week.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Cantor or reader: The Responsorial Psalm appointed for the day.
segments.label: Cantor or reader

segments.text: We respond: Repeat the Psalm refrain announced by the cantor or printed in the worship aid.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: Readings for the celebration: Find the assigned Scripture readings, Psalm response, and Gospel acclamation for the day.
segments.label: Readings for the celebration

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The Psalm response changes. Listen to its first presentation rather than assuming the same words each week.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? A deacon or priest proclaims a passage from Matthew, Mark, Luke, or John.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Encounter Jesus in his words, actions, death, and Resurrection. Imagine yourself among those who hear him: what attracts you, unsettles you, or invites a response?
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Remain standing as you are able. Make the small crosses on forehead, lips, and chest, asking that the Gospel shape your mind, words, and heart.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Deacon or priest: The Lord be with you.
segments.label: Deacon or priest

segments.text: We respond: And with your spirit.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: Deacon or priest, names the Gospel writer: A reading from the holy Gospel according to _____.
segments.label: Deacon or priest · names the Gospel writer

segments.text: We respond: Glory to you, O Lord.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: Deacon or priest: Proclaims the assigned Gospel passage.
segments.label: Deacon or priest

segments.text: Deacon or priest, conclusion: The Gospel of the Lord.
segments.label: Deacon or priest · conclusion

segments.text: We respond: Praise to you, Lord Jesus Christ.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: Readings for the celebration: Find the assigned Scripture readings, Psalm response, and Gospel acclamation for the day.
segments.label: Readings for the celebration

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The Gospel passage changes. Make the small crosses on forehead, lips, and chest at the opening announcement.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The community prays for the Church, the world, people in need, and the local community.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Let your prayer widen beyond those you already know. Intercession can develop attention to suffering and lead naturally to service, advocacy, and generosity.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Join the parish response. Include someone whose needs you have overlooked, and consider how you could help.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Priest: Introduces the Universal Prayer.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: Deacon or reader: Announces each prayer intention.
segments.label: Deacon or reader

segments.text: We respond, a common example: Lord, hear our prayer.
segments.label: We respond · a common example

segments.text: Priest: Concludes the petitions with a prayer.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: We respond: Amen.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The intentions and congregational response vary. Use the response announced at your parish; the example is not required at every Mass.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The priest leads the great prayer of thanksgiving, with the assembly joining through its acclamations.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? The Church gives thanks for God’s saving work, remembers Christ’s Paschal mystery, and intercedes for the living and the dead. This is a sacrificial memorial of Christ’s one offering, not a new crucifixion.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Listen to the whole prayer. Join the acclamations and follow the parish’s posture guidance, with accommodation for health and mobility.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words: The opening dialogue is followed by the Preface and the rest of the Eucharistic Prayer.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Priest: The Lord be with you.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: We respond: And with your spirit.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: Priest: Lift up your hearts.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: We respond: We lift them up to the Lord.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: Priest: Let us give thanks to the Lord our God.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: We respond: It is right and just.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: Priest: The Preface for the celebration.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: Priest: The chosen Eucharistic Prayer (I, II, III, IV, or another permitted prayer).
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The Sanctus, memorial acclamation, and Great Amen are the people’s responses within this prayer. Their lessons follow. Do not recite the priest’s parts with him.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The assembly acclaims the mystery of faith, and the Eucharistic Prayer continues.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Remembering Christ’s death and Resurrection gives hope beyond our present circumstances. The prayer also places us in relationship with the whole Church, including those who have died.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Join the acclamation printed in the worship aid. Listen as the prayer remembers the Church and entrusts people to God.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Priest: The mystery of faith.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text:
Everyone, option A: We proclaim your Death, O Lord,
and profess your Resurrection
until you come again.
segments.label: Everyone · option A

segments.text:
Everyone, option B: When we eat this Bread and drink this Cup,
we proclaim your Death, O Lord,
until you come again.
segments.label: Everyone · option B
Everyone · option C

segments.text: Priest: Continues the memorial, offering, and intercessions of the chosen Eucharistic Prayer.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. Use one approved acclamation, as led at your parish. The people do not say all three in sequence.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The Church prays for peace and unity, and a sign of peace may be exchanged.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Christ’s peace asks more of us than courtesy. Let this gesture call to mind the work of reconciliation that continues beyond the church doors.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Offer the sign calmly to those nearby, following local practice. Plan a step toward reconciliation where one is needed.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Priest: Prayer to Christ for the Church’s peace and unity.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: We respond: Amen.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: Priest: The peace of the Lord be with you always.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: We respond: And with your spirit.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: Deacon or priest, when used: Invites everyone to exchange a sign of peace.
segments.label: Deacon or priest · when used

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. There is no prescribed formula for each person’s personal exchange of peace. Follow your parish’s practice.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The community gives thanks in silence or song, followed by the prayer after Communion.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Prayer does not need to fill every moment with words. Rest in God’s presence and consider how what you have received can bear fruit through patience, compassion, and service.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Allow a few moments of quiet. Listen to the final prayer and join the Amen.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Everyone: Silent thanksgiving, or the appointed Communion hymn or song of praise.
segments.label: Everyone

segments.text: Priest: Let us pray.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: Priest: The Prayer after Communion appointed for the day.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: We respond: Amen.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. There is no fixed text for personal silent thanksgiving. The priest’s Prayer after Communion changes with the celebration.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The priest greets the assembly, which responds to him.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? A greeting at Mass expresses a relationship of worship and service. The community’s answer recognizes the minister’s role and joins the assembly in a common prayer.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? At the customary greeting, respond: “And with your spirit.” Listen to the dialogue as prayer, not merely an introduction.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Priest, one greeting option: The Lord be with you.
segments.label: Priest · one greeting option

segments.text: We respond: And with your spirit.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The priest may use another approved greeting; the people give the same response. A bishop may greet the assembly with a greeting of peace.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? After an invitation to pray and a brief silence, the priest voices the opening prayer.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Silence gives room for personal intentions before the common prayer. Learn to listen to its language: what does the Church ask of God, and what kind of life does that request invite?
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Offer an intention in the silence. Listen to the prayer and make its request your own through your Amen.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Priest: Let us pray.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: Everyone: A short silence for personal prayer.
segments.label: Everyone

segments.text: Priest: The Collect (opening prayer) appointed for this Mass.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: We respond: Amen.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The Collect changes with the day or occasion. The people listen to the priest’s prayer and give the concluding Amen.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? On Sundays and solemnities, the Second Reading comes from the New Testament: an apostolic letter or the Book of Revelation.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? The apostolic writings speak to communities learning to live the Gospel amid ordinary pressures. Ask how their encouragement and correction address your family, workplace, and parish.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Listen for a practical invitation. Respond “Thanks be to God” at the usual conclusion.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Reader: Proclaims the second reading assigned for the day.
segments.label: Reader

segments.text: Reader, conclusion: The word of the Lord.
segments.label: Reader · conclusion

segments.text: We respond: Thanks be to God.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: Readings for the celebration: Find the assigned Scripture readings, Psalm response, and Gospel acclamation for the day.
segments.label: Readings for the celebration

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. This reading is ordinarily included on Sundays and solemnities; many weekday Masses do not have it.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The ordained preacher reflects on the readings and the mystery being celebrated.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Keep listening for a connection between Scripture and your life. A useful question after the homily is what you can actually practice during the week.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Listen with openness. Write down one insight afterward and discuss it with your sponsor or formation group.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Priest or deacon: The homily: an explanation of the readings and the mystery being celebrated.
segments.label: Priest or deacon

segments.text: We listen: There is no prescribed congregational response at the end of the homily.
segments.label: We listen

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. A brief silence can follow. Do not add a response simply because another part of Mass uses it.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? Bread and wine are brought to the altar and prepared for the Eucharistic celebration.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Consider the human labor represented by these gifts. Your own work, service, struggles, and generosity can become an offering to God alongside the material gifts.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? During the preparation, quietly offer a part of your week. Connect your financial or practical support of the parish with care for people in need.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Priest: Blessing prayers over the bread and wine.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: We may respond, when said aloud: Blessed be God for ever.
segments.label: We may respond · when said aloud

segments.text: Deacon or priest, quietly: Prayer while mixing water and wine.
segments.label: Deacon or priest · quietly

segments.text: Priest, quietly: Prayer of humility and prayer at the washing of hands.
segments.label: Priest · quietly

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. If a song accompanies preparation, the blessing prayers are usually said quietly; there is no spoken response from the people at that point.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? Within the Eucharistic Prayer, the assembly joins a song of praise.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Holiness draws us toward awe, humility, and love. Worship gives us an opportunity to see beyond our own plans and recognize that life is held within God’s greater purpose.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Join the acclamation. Let praise lead into attentive silence as the prayer continues.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text:
Everyone, Sanctus: Holy, Holy, Holy Lord God of hosts.
Heaven and earth are full of your glory.
Hosanna in the highest.
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.
Hosanna in the highest.
segments.label: Everyone · Sanctus

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The same approved prayer is sung or recited. The whole acclamation includes praise of God’s holiness and the Hosanna.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The Eucharistic Prayer concludes in praise, and the people give their Amen.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Amen expresses assent: we make the prayer our own. Consider the relationship between what we affirm in worship and what we choose afterward.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Sing or say the Amen with the assembly. Notice that the Lord’s Prayer begins the Communion Rite that follows.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Priest: Through him, and with him, and in him, O God, almighty Father, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, all glory and honor is yours, for ever and ever.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: Everyone: Amen.
segments.label: Everyone

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. This is the Great Amen: the assembly’s assent to the entire Eucharistic Prayer. It may be sung.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The consecrated bread is broken, accompanied by the Lamb of God.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? The title Lamb of God recalls Christ’s self-giving love. The broken bread invites reflection on the unity of a community nourished by the one Lord.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Join the litany and ask for mercy and peace. Observe the parish’s posture directions as you are able.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text:
Everyone, Lamb of God: Lamb of God, you take away the sins of the world,
have mercy on us.
Lamb of God, you take away the sins of the world,
have mercy on us.
Lamb of God, you take away the sins of the world,
grant us peace.
segments.label: Everyone · Lamb of God

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. The invocation asking for mercy is ordinarily repeated twice; the final invocation asks for peace. The invocations may continue as needed while the bread is broken.
segments.label: Prayer notes

segments.text: What happens? The priest blesses the people before they depart.
segments.label: What happens?

segments.text: Why does it matter? Receive the blessing as encouragement for the life to which God calls you. Ask for the grace to carry patience, courage, and mercy into the ordinary places of your week.
segments.label: Why does it matter?

segments.text: What do I do? Receive the blessing prayerfully and make the Sign of the Cross when appropriate.
segments.label: What do I do?

segments.text: Now, pray with the Church using these words.
segments.label: What we say

segments.text: Priest: The Lord be with you.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: We respond: And with your spirit.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: Priest: May almighty God bless you, the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
segments.label: Priest

segments.text: We respond: Amen.
segments.label: We respond

segments.text: A note about this part of Mass. A solemn blessing or prayer over the people may be used instead. Listen to the instructions and respond Amen at the appropriate conclusions.
segments.label: Prayer notes
